subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should OpenClaw land a bounded internal cache for provider-normalized tool schema parameters now, or defer this issue to the broader prepared-runtime migration?
rationale: The repeated-normalization path is source-visible, but the permanent cache boundary affects provider hook ownership, plugin metadata lifecycle, custom provider behavior, and the prepared-runtime rollout.

options.title: Land a narrow internal cache
options.body: Refresh or replace the open cache PR with the bounded shape that caches cloned schema parameters for known safe provider hooks while rebuilding tool objects and closures per turn.

options.title: Defer to prepared runtime
options.body: Keep this issue open until the prepared-runtime rollout carries enough provider/tool facts to remove repeated hot-path work without a separate cache layer.

options.title: Require live repro first
options.body: Hold implementation until current-main Google/Gemini or heap proof shows the user-visible impact still occurs on a real provider path.

recommendation.title: Land a narrow internal cache
recommendation.body: Refresh or replace the open cache PR with the bounded shape that caches cloned schema parameters for known safe provider hooks while rebuilding tool objects and closures per turn.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision overlaps the prepared-runtime migration boundary and provider handle lifecycle tracked by mcaxtr.
